source.title: Innocence in the Crossfire: Roles of Skip Connections in Jailbreaking Visual Language Models
source.authors: Palash Nandi; M. Joshi; Tanmoy Chakraborty

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a positively framed response start changes harmful-output attack success in visual language models. It uses a different method and metric from the original sources: prompt manipulation and 2-ASR, not fine-tuning or per-token KL measurement.
record.gate_note: Rows record comparisons of positive-start setups 001 vs 000 and 101 vs 100, with and without SKIP-CON, because these directly vary the positive response cue and report 2-ASR. Other combinations involving in-context examples are not included: the table extraction is flattened and does not support reliable assignment of all per-model values to conditions. The study's layer-wise representation plots and SKIP-CON results are not evidence about fine-tuning, per-token KL concentration, or safety localization in weights.
record.test_reason: The study measures how a positively framed response start changes harmful-output rate (2-ASR) in three VLMs, a new setting for V4's 'getting past the opening' claim. It uses no fine-tuning, KL or weight analysis. The text is ambiguous on whether the cue is prefilled in the assistant turn or appended to the prompt ('appending the prompt with a positive response cue').
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors also state that visual descriptions help jailbreaks more than positive start phrases, and that with SKIP-CON the generalized-toxic in-context examples matter most. They frame SKIP-CON as a novel jailbreak method.
record.recipe_differences: Uses prompt manipulations and a layer-to-layer skip connection in visual language models, rather than fine-tuning aligned language models or measuring aligned/base per-token KL.
record.method_sensitivity: The positive-start outcome varies with visual category, model, presence of SKIP-CON, and whether a visual description is also included.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a scaled skip connection between two internal layers (SKIP-CON) raises 2-ASR, by up to 55 points for LLaVA-M, even with benign images.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perturbing internal layer routing in VLMs weakens refusal of harmful multimodal queries.

record.problems: The outcome is 2-ASR, a two-stage measure using refusal-phrase detection and Llama-Guard-3-1B rather than a direct human assessment of harmfulness. The paper reports averages over ten runs but no uncertainty estimates. The reported positive-start effects are mixed and often small.
record.rows_left_out: Table II and Sections VII.B-VIII.C report additional combinations involving self-reflective or generalized-toxic in-context examples. Those flattened table entries were not extracted because per-model values could not be assigned reliably across all conditions. Other SKIP-CON configuration results were left out because they do not isolate the positive-start comparison.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models; the layer-wise probing concerns input representations, not response positions.
Suffixes and decoding changes are not tested; there is no variation in prefill length, and it is unclear whether the cue is a true assistant-turn prefill.
No weight or rank localization of safety.
No analysis of data or objective causes.

record.verdict_notes: The parentheticals in the record's value fields are SKIP-CON gains copied from Table I, not positive-start effects. SKIP-CON rows are moved to none because the model is internally altered by the authors' attack. 2-ASR uses refusal-phrase matching plus Llama-Guard-3-1B, averaged over ten runs with no uncertainty reported. The position of the 'positive start' (prompt vs assistant prefill) is not specified, which weakens its mapping to V4.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on safety.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
The study tests positively framed response starts, but not suffixes, decoding changes, or the effect of a specified number of prefixed compliant tokens.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or training objectives produce safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and whether that training holds up.

relation.reason: Its controlled comparisons measure whether adding a positive response cue increases harmful responses, bearing directly on V4.

tranche.reason: Tests positive response cues and harmful-output rates in a new multimodal setting.

source_check.notes: Positive cues are described as appended to prompts; literal assistant-turn prefilling is not established. Scores average ten runs; no uncertainty establishes that one-point changes are negligible, and the paper's reported percentage gains represent percentage-point differences.
